html:
The Kaytetye are an Aboriginal Australian people of Central Australia, around Barrow Creek in the Northern Territory, north of Alice Springs. The map shows them as Kaytej from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours were the Alyawarre to the east, the Anmatyerre to the south and the Warumungu to the north. In 1872 the Overland Telegraph Line put a station at Barrow Creek on their land. In 1874 Kaytetye men attacked the station and killed two of its staff, and police and settler parties then killed many Kaytetye in reprisal. More of their people died in the Coniston massacre of 1928.
